chapters.summary: Paul declares that the gospel is the power of God unto salvation for everyone who believes, and points out that humanity, because of sin, stands in need of the righteousness of God.
keyPoints: Paul calls himself a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, and set apart to preach the gospel of God.

The gospel was promised beforehand by God through his prophets, concerning his Son Jesus Christ, who was of the seed of David according to the flesh, and declared to be the Son of God according to the Spirit of holiness.
The gospel is the power of God unto salvation for everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek, revealing the righteousness of God from faith to faith.
chapters.application: Today, are you convinced that the gospel is the power of God? Whatever your circumstances, respond to God's call in faith, and boldly proclaim this good news of salvation.

chapters.summary: Paul points out that though the Jews possess the law, they too have sinned, showing that God judges according to the heart, not by outward appearance.
keyPoints: Whoever judges another is guilty of the same things, and cannot escape the judgment of God.
The goodness of God is meant to lead people to repentance, yet hard and impenitent hearts only store up wrath for themselves.
True circumcision is a matter of the heart, in the spirit, not in the letter of the law.
chapters.application: Do not be so quick to judge others - examine yourself first. God values honesty of heart, so let us humbly receive his goodness and live lives that are the same inside as out.

chapters.summary: This chapter shows that Jews and Gentiles alike are under sin, yet God's faithfulness and righteousness remain unchanged; it is only by faith that anyone is justified, receiving grace through the redemption that is in Christ.
keyPoints: The advantage of the Jew is that they were entrusted with the very words of God, yet sin has made everyone equal before him.
God's judgment of the world is just, and human unrighteousness only serves to display God's own righteousness more clearly.
All have sinned and come short of the glory of God, and it is only by faith in Jesus Christ that anyone is justified.
chapters.application: Acknowledge your own insufficiency, and do not boast in your own works, but rest entirely on Christ's redemption. Receive God's grace each day by faith, and do good in love, to the glory of God.

chapters.summary: This chapter uses Abraham as an example to explain the truth of justification by faith, showing that it is faith, not works, that God counts as righteousness.
keyPoints: Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness - not because of anything he did.
David too pronounces a blessing on the one to whom God credits righteousness apart from works.
Abraham was justified by faith while still uncircumcised, showing that salvation reaches every nation.
chapters.application: We are not saved by good works, but by faith receiving the grace of God. When your faith grows weak, remember Abraham, and stand firm in trusting God's promises - he will surely fulfill them.

chapters.summary: This chapter describes the peace and hope that come from justification by faith, and the grace of Christ's redemption, which far surpasses the trespass of Adam.
keyPoints: Being justified by faith, we have peace with God and have gained entrance into his grace.
Suffering produces perseverance, and hope does not put us to shame.
The contrast between Adam's sin and Christ's grace shows how much more abundant the gift of salvation is.
chapters.application: Today, whatever you are going through, remember that God has already given you peace and hope. Depend on him in your suffering, and he will surely strengthen you.

chapters.summary: This chapter explains that believers, united with Christ through faith, have died to sin and now live to God - no longer slaves of sin, but slaves of righteousness.
keyPoints: Believers are baptized into Christ, united with him in his death and resurrection, and their old self has been crucified with him.
Sin shall no longer be master over believers, for they are not under the law, but under grace.
We are to offer ourselves to God as instruments of righteousness, and the end is eternal life - for the wages of sin is death.
themes: Slaves of Sin, Slaves of Righteousness
chapters.application: Remind yourself each day that you have died with Christ, and sin no longer has power over you. Offer yourself to God, live a holy life, and receive with gratitude the gift of eternal life.

chapters.summary: Paul explains that believers, through Christ, have been released from bondage to the law to serve in the newness of the Spirit, and he lays bare the inner struggle between good and evil.
keyPoints: Through the death of Christ, believers have died to the law, so that they might belong to the risen Christ.
The law itself is holy and just and good, but sin seizes the opportunity the commandment gives to produce sin in us.
Paul describes the war between the flesh and the mind, admitting that he cannot overcome it by his own strength.
chapters.application: When we struggle against sin, let us remember that Christ has already set us free - we no longer rely on our own strength, but on the Spirit. Look to Jesus for deliverance each day, and find peace in him.

chapters.summary: This chapter shows that believers in Christ are no longer condemned; by the Spirit they put to death the deeds of the flesh, become children of God, and can be assured that all things work together for good, so that in the end they are more than conquerors.
keyPoints: There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, for the law of the Spirit of life has set us free.
To set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.
We have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, and by the Spirit we put to death the deeds of the body, and so we will live.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, remember that God causes all things to work together for good to those who love him. By the Spirit, choose each day to set your mind on the Spirit, and live out peace and hope.

chapters.summary: Paul grieves over Israel's unbelief, explains the sovereignty and mercy of God's election, and shows that the Gentiles have attained righteousness by faith, while Israel failed to attain it by pursuing the law.
keyPoints: Paul is deeply grieved for his own people, the Israelites, and says he could wish himself accursed for their sake.
God's sovereign election is made clear - it depends not on human works, but on him who calls.
The Gentiles have attained righteousness by faith, while Israel has stumbled by pursuing it through the law.
chapters.application: Pray for the family and friends who do not yet know the Lord, trusting in God's absolute sovereignty and mercy. Humbly receive his grace, and do not boast in your own works.

chapters.summary: This chapter explains that Israel rejected Christ by seeking a righteousness based on the law, but the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ brings salvation to everyone who calls on the name of the Lord - and the gospel has now been proclaimed to all peoples.
keyPoints: Paul prays for Israel's salvation, because though they have a zeal for God, it is not based on true knowledge.
Paul contrasts the righteousness of the law with the righteousness of faith, emphasizing that salvation comes through trusting in Christ.
Whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved - but they must first hear and believe, and someone must be sent to preach the good news.
chapters.application: Today let us pray for those who do not yet believe, and actively proclaim the gospel - for how can people believe if they have never heard? May the Lord give us a heart and a voice for preaching, so that more may be justified by faith.

chapters.summary: Paul discusses God's plan of salvation for Israel, explaining that Israel's stumbling has brought salvation to the Gentiles, but that in the end all Israel will be saved.
keyPoints: God has not cast away Israel; a remnant still remains.
The Gentiles have been grafted into the olive tree by faith, and so have no reason to boast.
Israel's present disobedience is temporary, and will in the end bring about the salvation of the whole nation.
chapters.application: Do not become proud of your identity as a believer. Instead, live with reverence and gratitude, for how vast is God's grace. Let us accept one another and wait for the Lord to bring his plan to completion.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to offer their bodies as a living sacrifice, to be united in Christ, and to live out their faith with love and humility.
keyPoints: Offering our bodies as a living sacrifice is holy service, acceptable and pleasing to God.
Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may know God's will.
In Christ we are members of one another, serving according to the gifts we have been given, and treating one another with love.
chapters.application: Today, let us offer ourselves to God as a living sacrifice, serving others in love at home and at work, refusing to be swept along by the crowd, and living out the likeness of Christ.

chapters.summary: Paul teaches believers to submit to those in authority, since all authority comes from God, and to love their neighbor as themselves, living out the deeds of light.
keyPoints: Submit to those in authority, for authority is established by God, and to resist it is to resist God.
Pay your taxes and fulfill your civic duties with a clear conscience, for those in authority are God's servants.
Love is the fulfilling of the law; put on the Lord Jesus Christ, cast off the deeds of darkness, and walk decently.
chapters.application: In everyday life, let us respect the law and those in authority, while treating our neighbors with love, living out a witness of light that brings glory to God.

chapters.summary: Paul teaches believers to accept one another, and not to judge a brother over secondary matters like food or the observance of days, since each person lives for the Lord and will ultimately give an account to him.
keyPoints: Accept the one whose faith is weak, without quarreling over disputable matters.
Whether observing a day or eating meat, it is done unto the Lord, so we must not look down on or judge one another.
The kingdom of God is not a matter of food and drink, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit - so let us pursue what makes for peace.
chapters.application: In daily life, respect each person's own relationship with the Lord, and do not let small matters cause disputes. Keep peace and the building up of others in mind, to the glory of God.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to follow the example of Christ, not seeking to please themselves, but accepting one another and glorifying God with one mind, and he shares his own calling and plans to preach the gospel to the Gentiles.
keyPoints: We who are strong ought to bear with the weaknesses of the weak, not seeking to please ourselves, but following the example of Christ.
Christ accepted us, so that we too should accept one another, just as Christ accepted us, to the glory of God.
Paul explains that Christ became a servant to the Jews, and that the gospel was also preached to the Gentiles, so that they too might glorify God for his mercy.
chapters.application: In your daily life, show understanding toward those who are weak, not seeking your own advantage. Have the mind of Christ, accept people who are different from you, and glorify God together with one mind.

chapters.summary: In this final chapter of Romans, Paul commends Phebe and sends greetings to many believers in the Roman church, stressing mutual acceptance and united service in the Lord.
keyPoints: Paul commends Phebe, a deaconess of the church, and asks the believers to help her.
Paul lists many fellow workers, showing how closely connected the members of the church are to one another.
Paul warns believers to watch out for those who cause division and turn people from the faith, and urges them to continue doing good.
chapters.application: Today let us honor and support one another in the Lord, while remaining watchful to guard the purity of our faith, bearing witness to Christ with both love and wisdom.
